content: Ethambutol is an antibiotic used in combination with other medications to treat tuberculosis (TB). It is effective only against bacterial infections and does not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu. How to Use: Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor. It is usually taken once daily, but in some cases, it may be prescribed to be taken twice weekly. Follow your doctor’s instructions precisely. For optimal effectiveness, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking this medication, along with other TB medications, for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve or disappear. Side Effects: Common side effects may include headache, loss of appetite, upset stomach, nausea, or vomiting. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor. Precautions: Before taking ethambutol, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Ethambutol may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication, as it may increase the risk of liver disease. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It passes into breast milk but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. However, if you have HIV, breastfeeding may transmit the virus to your baby. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Monitoring: While taking this medication, you may need regular lab and medical tests, such as sputum tests, eye/vision exams, kidney and liver function tests, and complete blood counts. Ensure you attend all medical and lab appointments. Missed Dose: It is important to take each dose as scheduled. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
